```{python}
from pathlib import Path
from pyprojroot import here
import os
import subprocess

# for reading/writing TOML and YAML
import tomllib
import tomli_w
import yaml

# for pretty in-notebook displays
from rich.console import Console
from rich.panel import Panel
from rich.columns import Columns
from rich.syntax import Syntax

# for interacting with a singularity image
from spython.main import Client
from spython.main.parse.recipe import Recipe
from spython.main.parse.writers import SingularityWriter

console = Console()
```

To begin, we need to select a base Linux distribution for the platform 
image. The platform image is a singularity container that contains everything
needed to run the project.

It can be helpful to think of this as building a computer from scratch using
a file tree. The base image is the operating system, including all
the things you see in locations like `/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/lib`, 
`/usr/lib`, etc. Selecting a "platform image" means picking the Linux
version that fills all of those directories with the right versions
of the right libraries. We can also put additional things into
that image by configuring installation recipes with tools like
Spack or `dnf`, as well as using data science languages like
R and Python and their package managers. Most importantly,
though, is the understanding that we will bind the project
as-is into the container at runtime.

What this means is that we can achieve a Singularity image 
capable of running the specific R and Python packages that
the project needs, without having to worry about how to rebuild
the whole stack. Sure, environments can still break, but because
we are recording how we arrived at the built image, its dependency
tree, and the project specific R and Python environments, we 
can always rebuild the image from scratch if necessary. The
project-specific Spack and R/Python installations are defined 
in the project repository and activated from `/work`, so that
when we share the container with others, it doesn't come with
the deterministically built project already run — instead, it comes with
a guarantee that _when_ the project is bound into the container, 
it will be able to install the project dependencies as needed and run the project code.

## Project configuration

Change the base image if necessary, but in general, our work is done 
on Rocky Linux 8 with Spack. This is because the FASRC cluster is built on Rocky Linux 8,
and Spack is a very common and powerful package manager for HPC, serving as
an academia-focused drop-in replacement for things like `anaconda`. 
A base image from the Spack registry is therefore used to bootstrap the platform image.

```{python}
BASE_IMAGE = "docker://spack/rockylinux8:develop"
```

Here, we'll define some more top level project variables.

```{python}
# project variables
PROJECT_NAME = "prospectorMahery"
PROJECT_DIR = Path("/n/holylabs/LABS/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors") / PROJECT_NAME
WORKBENCH_DIR = here()
RUNTIME_DIR = WORKBENCH_DIR / "projects" / PROJECT_NAME

TMP_SANDBOX = Path(f"/tmp/{os.environ['USER']}-{PROJECT_NAME}-sandbox")


SINGULARITY_DEF = PROJECT_DIR / ".devcontainer" / "Singularity.def"
SINGULARITY_SIF = PROJECT_DIR / ".devcontainer" / "Singularity.sif"

CONTAINER_HOME = PROJECT_DIR / ".container-home"

RPROJECT_TOML_PATH = PROJECT_DIR / "rproject.toml"
PYPROJECT_TOML_PATH = PROJECT_DIR / "pyproject.toml"

SUBMITIT_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "slurm" / "submitit"

for path in [
    RUNTIME_DIR,
    SINGULARITY_DEF.parent,
    SUBMITIT_DIR,
    CONTAINER_HOME,
]:
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

These elements are pretty simple!

## 3. Build a disposable sandbox

We start with a temporary sandbox — this is where we experiment. The sandbox is node-local 
and disposable, meaning nothing that we do in here is persisted. The point is to
try out different package installs (specified above) and see if they work 
_before_ we commit to a final SIF.

```{python}
#| eval: false
Client.build(
    image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
    recipe=BASE_IMAGE,
    options=["--fakeroot", "--sandbox", "--fix-perms", "--force"],
    sudo=False,
)
```

Inspect the base image.

```{python}
#| eval: false
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        "ls /",
        image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
        writable=True,
    )
)
```

Create `/work`.

```{python}
#| eval: false
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        "mkdir -p /work && ls -ld /work",
        image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
        writable=True,
    )
)
```

Bind the project into `/work`.

```{python}
#| eval: false
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        "ls -l /work",
        image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
        writable=True,
        bind_project=True,
    )
)
```

Decision: `/work` is the runtime contract. The project will be bound here. The image should create the mount point, but the project itself should not be copied into the image.

If there are any project specific, but explicitly base image dependencies, they 
should be added to the list below. For everything otherwise, the project will be 
bound into `/work` at runtime and the project specific dependencies will be 
installed from the `rproject.toml` and `pyproject.toml` files.






















## 5. Define the platform image recipe

The platform image owns:

- Rocky/Spack base
- OS build dependencies
- `/work` mount point
- `rv`
- `arf`
- general developer tools

The project owns:

- `spack.yaml`
- `rproject.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`
- source code
- runtime package state under `/work`

We're implementing a simple `dataclass` for installable platform elements.
This will make it easy for us to add/remove elements from the platform 
image without having to rewrite the whole recipe several times over.

```{python}
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional

@dataclass
class Installable:
    name: str
    kind: str  # "dnf", "binary", "spack", "cargo", "script"
    commands: list[str]
    path: Optional[str] = None
    test: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def install_lines(self) -> list[str]:
        return self.commands

    def test_lines(self) -> list[str]:
        return self.test
```

So, for example, our favourite R console, `arf`, can be represented like so:

```{python}
arf_pkg = Installable(
    name="arf",
    kind="cargo",
    path="/root/.cargo/bin/arf",
    commands=[
        "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/eitsupi/arf/releases/latest/download/arf-console-installer.sh | sh",
        """
        ARF_BIN="$(find /root/.cargo/bin /home -path '*/.cargo/bin/arf' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
        if [ -z "$ARF_BIN" ]; then
            ARF_BIN="$(find / -path '*/.cargo/bin/arf' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
        fi

        test -n "$ARF_BIN"
        install -m 0755 "$ARF_BIN" /usr/local/bin/arf
        """
    ]
)
```

To get the platform image system dependencies, we might want to use 
`pak::pkg_sysreqs()` in R or `pip check` in Python.

For now, we will just add the OS-level build dependencies that we know about.

```{python}
recipe = Recipe()
recipe.fromHeader = "spack/rockylinux8:develop"

recipe.install = [
    "set -eux",
    "dnf install -y curl ca-certificates tar gzip",
    "dnf install -y epel-release",
    
] + arf_pkg.install_lines()

recipe.environ = [
    "PATH=/usr/local/bin:/opt/views/view/bin:/root/.cargo/bin:/usr/cargo/bin:$PATH",
    "SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true",
    "SPACK_USER_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/spack-user-config",
    "SPACK_USER_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/spack-user-cache",
    "SPACK_MISC_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/spack-misc-cache",
]

recipe.test = [
    "echo $PATH",
    "rv --version",
    "arf --version",
    "which spack",
]
```

Export the recipe.

```{python}
#| eval: false
writer = SingularityWriter({"spython-base": recipe})
definition = writer.convert()
print(definition)
SINGULARITY_DEF.write_text(definition)
```

## 7. Install and validate project environment in the sandbox

```{python}
#| eval: false
write_spack_yaml()
write_rproject_toml()

show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        """
        export SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true

        . /opt/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh
        cd /work

        spack env activate -d .
        spack concretize
        spack install --deprecated --fail-fast -j12 --no-checksum

        rv sync || true
        """,
        writable=True,
        bind_project=True,
    ),
    tail=120,
)
```

If package installation fails, inspect the error, add the missing system library to either:

- `recipe.install`, if it is an OS-level build dependency
- `spack_env["spack"]["specs"]`, if it should be managed by Spack
- `rproject["project"]["dependencies"]`, if it is an R package

Then write the files and retry.

## 8. Final sitrep

```{python}
#| eval: false
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        """
        export SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true

        . /opt/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh
        cd /work
        spack env activate -d .

        echo $PATH
        echo "Sitrep:"
        echo "code-server:" $(which code-server)
        echo "R:" $(which R)
        echo "Python:" $(which python)
        echo "rv:" $(which rv)
        echo "arf:" $(which arf)
        """,
        writable=True,
        bind_project=True,
    )
)
```

Decision: once this passes, stop mutating the sandbox. Export the recipe and build the final project SIF.

## 9. Build final SIF with submitit

```{python}
#| eval: false
import submitit

n_cpus = 12

executor = submitit.AutoExecutor(folder=str(SUBMITIT_DIR / "%j"))

executor.update_parameters(
    timeout_min=360,
    slurm_partition="hsph",
    mem_gb=32.0,
    cpus_per_task=n_cpus,
    slurm_job_name=f"build-{PROJECT_NAME}-container",
)
```

```{python}
#| eval: false
def build_container():
    from spython.main import Client
    from pathlib import Path

    singularity_sif = Path("SINGULARITY_SIF_PLACEHOLDER")
    singularity_def = Path("SINGULARITY_DEF_PLACEHOLDER")

    return Client.build(
        image=str(singularity_sif),
        recipe=str(singularity_def),
        options=["--fakeroot", "--force"],
        sudo=False,
    )
```

Patch placeholders before submission.

```{python}
#| eval: false
build_container.__globals__["SINGULARITY_SIF_PLACEHOLDER"] = str(SINGULARITY_SIF)
build_container.__globals__["SINGULARITY_DEF_PLACEHOLDER"] = str(SINGULARITY_DEF)

job = executor.submit(build_container)
job.job_id
```

```{python}
#| eval: false
show_submitit_job(job)
```

## 10. Runtime command

The SIF is read-only. Do not launch it with `--writable`.

At runtime, bind the project into `/work`, activate the project Spack environment, install/update project dependencies as needed, and then launch `code-server` or run the pipeline.

```{python}
runtime_command = [
    "export SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true",
    ". /opt/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh",
    "cd /work",
    "spack env activate -d .",
    "spack concretize",
    "spack install --deprecated --fail-fast -j12 --no-checksum",
    "rv sync || true",
    "code-server --bind-addr 0.0.0.0:${PORT:-8026} /work",
]
runtime_command
```

A launch script can be generated later from this list, or executed through a Python/Slurm interface. The important runtime contract is:

```bash
singularity exec \
  --no-home \
  --bind "$PROJECT_DIR:/work" \
  "$SINGULARITY_SIF" \
  bash --noprofile --norc -lc '<runtime command>'
```
